title: Shimon ben Antiphras
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: It is told in [Derekh Eretz Rabbah, beginning of chapter 6](https://www.sefaria.org/Tractate_Derekh_Eretz_Rabbah.6.1), that they told Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai that he [Shimon ben Antiphras] would feed and give drink to all the guests who came to him, but at the time of their departure he would flog them. He [Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai] sent Rabbi Yehoshua to him. When he arrived, he said to him, “Peace upon you, Rabbi.” He said to him, “I need a lodging.” He said to him, “Stay in peace.” They sat and engaged in Torah until evening. Afterward he escorted him (and did not flog him). He said to him, “Why have I heard about you that you flog the guests, yet you did not flog me?” He said to him, “Rabbi, you are a great sage and you have good manners. As for the people who come to me, I decreed that they should eat, but they vow by the Torah and transgress [their vows not to eat].” He said to him, “Blessed are you to Heaven for having done so.”[^1][^2]

notes.text: The parallel spells the host’s name Antipatros.
Hyman has ור״א יש בך; the parallel reads ודרך ארץ יש בידך, ‘you have good manners.’ It also explains that the guests vowed not to eat or drink and then did so.
